scope: Initial executable synchronous numeric/Bool recursive record and enum source subset

implementation.admission: Independent frontend and executable-IR checks require finite construction bases and scalar numeric/Bool or direct nominal record fields
implementation.matching: Recursive enum matches remain explicit in typed IR and lower through flat scf.index_switch with validated tags and branch-local frames
implementation.values: Checked construction, field/pattern reads, direct recursion, immutable record updates, shared child references and recursive results use managed backing
implementation.separation: Acyclic enum control lowering is unchanged; recursive continuation/worker plans and CPU bridge exports remain rejected
implementation.diagnostics: Unconstructible cycles identify a nonconstructible dependency field rather than an unrelated finite leaf

coverage: All ten numeric widths plus Bool fields
Exact uint64 and float64 payload values
Lists and binary trees with multiple recursive edges
Mutual records/enums and immutable record updates
Shared nested tails, recursive function results and conditional/match-returned values
Wildcard/single-case/nested matches, branch isolation and imports
Allocation failure at each publication in a 32-node returned list
Checked arithmetic faults and native call-limit cleanup
Malformed typed-match metadata rejected before backend memory/type access
Existing semantic, nested-record, enum and managed-payload regressions
qualification.format: New C++ files pass clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Initial recursive compilation units restrict all nominal fields to scalar numeric/Bool or direct nominal links
String/collection/callable fields, record arrays and application-error channels remain unsupported in recursive units
Callable values, parallel groups, workers, continuation planning, placement/GPU and CPU bridge exports remain rejected
Direct recursion retains the existing checked native-call budget; no tail-call or heap-stack optimization added
Enums retain constructor/match replacement semantics; with updates apply to plain records
